messages:
maria (runtime): Quick follow-up on the kernel-autotune RFC. I prototyped a lightweight heuristic for seq-len bucketing + batch-shape selection + warmup. Sharing results and tradeoffs, want opinions.

jon (mlopt): Nice. Can you paste the config you tested?

maria (runtime): Sure — prototype cfg (simplified):
```yaml
autotune:
  buckets: [8, 32, 128, 512]
  batch_shapes:
    - {max_seq: 32, max_batch: 16}
    - {max_seq: 128, max_batch: 8}
    - {max_seq: 512, max_batch: 2}
  warmup_runs: 3  # micro-batches to execute before marking kernel as warm
  eviction_threshold: 0.2  # relative perf drop to evict pref kernel
```

sophie (eng): How did you pick the bucket boundaries? 8/32/128 seems coarse.

maria (runtime): Two reasons: 1) empirical latency cliffs around 8 and 32 for our optimized attention kernels on Ampere/A100; 2) reduces combinatorial batch-shape space. We saw diminishing returns below factor-of-4 buckets.

jon (mlopt): Also important: batch shape config should be workload-driven. For chat workloads we should bias for small seq, higher batch; synchronous inference (LLama-style) prefers bigger seq, smaller batch.

kevin (infra): Is the tuner per-GPU-type or global? We can't have a shared global because kernel perf varies with sm count and memory bandwidth.

maria (runtime): Per-device-class. Tuner keys: (arch, compute_cap, driver_version, quant_profile). We persist best kernel per bucket and batch-shape pair.

maria (runtime): Warmup semantics: for first N requests of a new (bucket, kernel) pair we run warmup_runs micro-batches with same shapes; track P50/P95 and token throughput. If warm metrics >= baseline*0.95 we mark warm.

tomas (sre): Curious about cost of warmups at scale. Can warmup storms overload nodes?

maria (runtime): Good call. We gate warmups by node-util and only allow concurrent warmups <= 1 per GPU. Also backoff (exponential) if warmup causes latency SLO violation.

jon (mlopt): What signals do we use to choose kernel? raw latency vs tokens/sec? Might need different objective for hosted vs dedicated.

maria (runtime): We expose objective selection: latency-first (min P95), throughput-first (max tokens/sec), or cost-aware (weighted op_count / token). Default is latency-first for <250ms target, else throughput-first for batchy workloads.

kevin (infra): How does KV cache factor in? Cold KV cache will make short stability windows.

maria (runtime): We treat KV-warmed and KV-cold as separate dimensions. When a request hits with empty cache we label shape as cold and run cold-warmup probes. Cache-warm state decays after N idle seconds.

sophie (eng): Any thoughts on eviction? The eviction_threshold in config — how sensitive is it?

maria (runtime): We use rolling windows (5m) and require difference > eviction_threshold AND sustained for two consecutive windows to evict to avoid flapping. Also prefer not to evict kernels that are cheaper on cost metric even if slightly slower.

jon (mlopt): Did you test bucket misclassification costs? e.g., when seq length jumps from 30->120 mid-batch.

maria (runtime): Yes — we route by longest-seq in a batch. If mismatch, we fall back to a compatibility kernel (slower but safe). We log a routing_mismatch counter and trigger a canary if mismatch rate > 1% for 10m.

tomas (sre): For canaries, please emit a trace tag and make the fallback visible in Console (route.reason=fallback_kernel). Ops needs fast rollback.

maria (runtime): Agreed — added to action items. Also plan to surface per-route kernel histogram in Console.

deploy-bot: deployment started: autotune/proto v0.3 -> canary cluster (5 nodes).

kevin (infra): Can we limit warmups to canary nodes only until we validate?

maria (runtime): Done — warmups off on prod until canary passes 24h with <0.5% SLO impact.

sophie (eng): +1 on the cautious rollout. One more: add a lightweight simulation mode that scores kernels offline using traces to reduce warmup churn.

maria (runtime): Plan: (1) run offline scoring on last 24h traces (jon + sophie), (2) canary autotuner v0.3 with warmups limited, (3) surface metrics, (4) evaluate eviction sensitivity. Owners: jon (offline scoring), kevin (canary infra), maria (runtime changes), tomas (SLO monitoring).

jon (mlopt): I'll start trace scorer PR and push a small opt model to compare tokens/sec.

sophie (eng): I'll add route.metrics for kernel_selected and routing_mismatch.

kevin (infra): I'll whitelist canary nodes and set warmup concurrency to 1.

maria (runtime): Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge the proto and schedule canary tonight. :thumbsup:

jon (mlopt): :thumbsup:

sophie (eng): LGTM

kevin (infra): LGTM
